mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which pressures corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when RSAFS falls > 2% in 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production exceeding 0.5% signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 3% combined with a 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 10% signals severe demand weakness, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 3% in 3 months AND HOUST falls > 10% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when both RSAFS falls > 3% and HOUST falls > 10% in 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment above 0.5% combined with a monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 0.2% signals a tight labor market, which boosts wage pressures and input costs, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 1 month AND UNRATE falls < 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls < 0.2% in 1 month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 4% signals strengthening household demand, which expands corporate revenues and earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when RSAFS rises > 4% in 6 months (t-test p > 0.05).
